title: An unparseable sharedTime destroys the hearing three catch blocks deep

nodeEvidence.what: the defect as written in the register: `informantRegisters.find(register => register.registerDate)` then `.registerDate` on the result. UNREACHABLE AS WRITTEN — see the demonstration note below.

getLocalDateTime always returns a String — `moment.tz(...).format(...) + "Z"` — which for an unparseable input is the literal "Invalid dateZ". A non-empty String is truthy, so the .find at InformantRegisterSubscriptions/index.js:17 ALWAYS matches the first fragment and the TypeError at :18 cannot fire from this path.

THE REACHABLE TWIN: `const orderDate = new Date(on).toISOString().slice(0, 10);` sits OUTSIDE the try block, which only starts at line 41. `new Date("Invalid dateZ").toISOString()` throws RangeError: Invalid time value, and no catch in this function sees it.
the RangeError escapes to the activity catch, is logged, and the activity returns undefined.
`.length` on that undefined throws, and is swallowed. Same terminal silence as D6.

assertion: The input is the prosecution-case fixture, unmodified, with sharedTime "not-a-timestamp". Assert EXACTLY: (1) expected.json is JSON null — no documents; (2) meta.json observed.outcome is "swallowed-exception"; (3) observed.swallowedErrors mentions RangeError. Parity requirement for the Java port: zero documents. But the Java port MUST NOT get there by the Node route. Two things must be asserted about HOW: (a) an unparseable sharedTime must be rejected as a non-transient contract violation with a reason code, dead-lettered, and persisted FAILED — never allowed to travel through the pipeline as the string "Invalid dateZ"; (b) the string "Invalid date" must never appear in any field of any document the Java port emits. Sub-assertion (b) is the one that catches a lazy port: a Java implementation that mirrors moment's forgiving formatting will happily ship "Invalid dateZ" into a registerDate the frozen schema types as a date-time, exactly as Node does elsewhere (see s05-invalid-date-z-shipped-as-a-timestamp). Note for whoever maintains this: if someone "fixes" the Node-side D7 line, this case does not change at all — the case pins the reachable RangeError, not the unreachable TypeError.
demonstrationNote: D7 as written in the design register (a TypeError at InformantRegisterSubscriptions/index.js:18) is UNREACHABLE through the orchestrator, and the pack says so rather than inventing a case for it: SetInformantRegister/index.js:83 always assigns a non-empty String, so the .find always matches. What IS reachable — and is the same failure in the same region, "the register date is not usable" — is the RangeError at ReferenceDataService.js:38. That is what this case records.
